answer: An optical protocol curbs Sybil attacks in autonomous forestry swarms. Candidate nodes must clamp onto harvested cedar logs, measuring laser backscatter inside a velvet shroud while broadcasting a low-power acoustic whisper. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of fabricating and deploying dedicated robotic spectrometers per identity. However, residual sawdust skews optical baselines, causing occasional false rejections of honest agents.
